title: staggered-start-entropy-notes
content:
One-line summary:
  Intermittent capacity thrash during scheduled warm-starts of dedicated GPU pool. Symptoms: short bursts of pod creation/destruction, warm sessions failing healthchecks, overall reduced available capacity for ~60-90s windows. Observed during low-load evenings (UTC).

Hypothesis (current ordering prioritized):
  1) Staggered-start scheduling + cooldown logic mismatch: autoscaler ramps up N nodes but scheduler's warm handshake assumes immediate node readiness; when healthchecks are slow pods are deleted which triggers scale-down then re-up (oscillation).
  2) KV cache / model weight cache not being populated fast enough (prefix cache pressure) → extra latency causes probe timeouts → readiness false → pod bounce.
  3) Token-bucket leak on the dedicated pool circuit breaker: requests queued then spilled to fallback tier, causing short OLTP-like spikes that collision with warmup windows.
  4) Container runtime or driver edge-case (nvidia-driver v525 vs 530) causing intermittent GPU attach failures and transient OOMs.
  5) Controller reconcilers have an ordering bug: node label applied after daemonset is scheduled, causing daemonset to re-evaluate and kill warm pods.

Important timestamps / event snippets (UTC):
  2025-01-24T23:12:06 - first observed: 6 pods created in pool-dedicated-west-1; 4 pod restarts within 40s.
  2025-01-24T23:12:45 - autoscaler log: "scaleUp: requested 6 -> 12, reason: target_utilization_exceeded"
  2025-01-24T23:13:30 - scheduler log: "pod t-abc failed readiness: livenessProbe timeout after 10s"
  2025-01-24T23:14:10 - node kubelet: "Device plugin: gpu-attach succeeded" then 15s later "OOMKill: process worker (pid 2734)"

Commands I ran (snippets/paste-ready):
  # list warm pool pods and ages
  kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=warm -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
  OUTPUT: many with RESTARTS=1, AGE 20s-2m, NODE cycle between node-x-1 and node-x-3

  # inspect failing pod events
  kubectl -n dedicated describe pod t-abc
  EVENTS:
    Normal Scheduled   1m   default-scheduler   Successfully assigned dedicated/t-abc to node-x-1
    Warning Unhealthy  50s  kubelet              Readiness probe failed: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
    Normal Killing     48s  kubelet              Stopping container worker

  # check kubelet logs on node-x-1 (trimmed)
  journalctl -u kubelet -o cat | grep -E "Readiness probe failed|Device plugin|OOMKill" -n
    23:14:05 Device plugin: GPU attach succeeded for pod t-abc
    23:14:22 Readiness probe failed for pod t-abc: context deadline exceeded
    23:14:25 Kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2734 (worker)

  # autoscaler decisions (controller logs)
  kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/node-autoscaler -c autoscaler | tail -n 200
  SAMPLE: "scaleDown: candidateNodes=[node-x-5] reason=underutilized consecutiveUnneeded=2"

Prometheus queries used to correlate:
  - rate(gpu_utilization_seconds_total{pool="dedicated-west-1"}[1m])
  - avg_over_time(kube_pod_start_time_seconds{label_pool="warm"}[5m])
  - increases in container_restart_total by pod (filtered start times)
  Observed small spikes in gpu_utilization at exactly the same time as pod churn (likely due to fallback traffic).

Error snippets seen across different traces:
  "Readiness probe failed: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
  "OOMKill: process worker (pid 2734)"
  "device plugin: failed to allocate GPU memory: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY"
  "rpc: connection closed by peer" (between scheduler and warm handshake service)

Things tried so far (results):
  - Increased readinessProbe timeout from 10s -> 20s on warm pods (staged in canary): reduced immediate kills but still saw ~30% bounce for heavy models. (status: partial improvement)
  - Bumped autoscaler stabilization window from 30s -> 90s: oscillation amplitude dropped but still present during multi-pod warm events. Strange: scale-down still triggered when 1/3 pods were NotReady (autoscaler thought nodes were underutilized). (status: partial)
  - Added debug env to warm binary to log model load timings (time to mmap weights, time to init kv cache). Observed model weight mmap ~1100ms, kv-cache init 800–1200ms for TLR models. (status: informative)
  - Replayed a warm startup locally with strace: saw occasional 200ms pause waiting on /dev/nvhost-ctrl (suspicious driver syscall latency). (status: suspicious)
  - Forced node labels earlier in bootstrap path (change in node-init) during canary: didn't reproduce but smaller sample size. (status: inconclusive)
  - Throttle inbound admission to fallback tier during warm windows by increasing route weight for dedicated pool (edge-level traffic shaping): reduced GPU spikes but didn't eliminate probe failures. (status: mitigated symptoms)

Data points that rule out some causes:
  - Not purely scheduler QPS spike: control-plane latencies were normal in the time window per apiserver metrics.
  - Not docker daemon crash: container runtime logs show no restarts of containerd.

Open questions / things I want to validate quickly:
  - Is there a race between our daemonset that applies labels and the autoscaler snapshot logic? If snapshot is taken before label, nodes may be considered not part of pool briefly. How old are snapshots?
  - Are readiness probes hitting an endpoint that depends on the KV cache population? If yes, we need decoupled probe that only checks binary liveness + GPU attach.
  - Driver syscall latencies: is there a known regression in kernel/nvidia driver around 525->530 that matches 200ms waits? Any known issues with /dev/nvhost-ctrl?
  - What is the exact autoscaler logic for "consecutiveUnneeded" when some nodes are NotReady but still running pods? Might be incorrectly counting and allowing scaleDown.

Quick repro plan (low-risk):
  1) Canary change: change readiness probe handler to return "initializing" state for 30s then become Ready once weight mmap + minimal checkpoint loaded. This will decouple the readiness from full KV population. (ETA: 1h to patch + deploy)
  2) Enable verbose autoscaler debug for target pool for 12h window to capture decisions with node labels and pod NotReady counts (ETA: a few hours to collect logs).
  3) Instrument node-init to emit timestamp when label applied and when daemonset started. Correlate with autoscaler snapshots. (ETA: 3–4h)
  4) On a spare test pool, force start 10 warm instances in parallel and capture kernel traces (ftrace) around device attach to check nvhost latency. (needs infra SRE approval).

Notes about risk and customer impact:
  - This mostly affects Dedicated warm pool during scheduled ramps (batch warm-ups) — customers might see reduced headroom for short windows and higher tail latency if fallback tiers are used. Not a full outage, but could cause degraded throughput for short time.
  - Priority: medium-high (affects cost & SLOs for Dedicated).

Next steps / TODOs (owner assigned where applicable):
  - [Riley] implement decoupled readiness probe in warm binary and roll to canary (track success metric: probe-fail rate).
  - [Samir] enable autoscaler debug and collect logs for last 48h window (attach to ENGINF-4723).
  - [Elena] check known driver/kernel regressions and file a ticket with infra if nvhost syscall latency is confirmed.
  - [Marcus] run the parallel start test on test-pool-4 and capture ftrace (coordinate with SRE).

Random breadcrumbs / small observations (likely noise but saved anyway):
  - Saw one event where node reported Ready but kube-proxy iptables rules were briefly missing (10s window). Might be unrelated but could cause traffic blackhole for probes.
  - Some model variants (smaller quantized) warm ~300ms for mmap+kv versus TLR models 1.8s — suggests model size matters more than compute for warm handshake.
  - A handful of pods showed "rpc: connection closed by peer" from warm-handshake sidecar right before readiness false. Suspect sidecar has small connection buffer and is getting reset by kubelet when container gets OOMKilled — chicken/egg.

If I get time: assemble timeline with 1s granularity from kube-apiserver, kubelet, autoscaler, and warm binary logs and put into spreadsheet for visual correlation. Might be helpful to see exact ordering (which event precedes which) to decide whether autoscaler snapshot timing is root cause.

Notes to self: keep this doc informal — will extract into ENGINF ticket after repro steps validated. Avoid full-scale autoscaler parameter tweeks in prod without test-pool validation.

End of notes.
